title: Derived scalar adjunction and exact restriction for sheaf dg algebras
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra is a sheaf of associative unital graded $\mathcal O$-algebras with a degree-one differential satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. A right dg module satisfies $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$. For such an algebra $\mathcal R$, let $D(\mathcal R)$ be the homotopy category of right dg modules localized at maps inducing isomorphisms on all underlying cohomology sheaves; shifts and distinguished triangles are induced by shifts and mapping cones [def-weil-triangulated-category].

For every homomorphism $\varphi:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ of sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebras, these localized categories are triangulated, restriction $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}:D(\mathcal S)\to D(\mathcal R)$ is exact, and derived extension $L_{\varphi}(M)=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S$ exists, is exact, and is left adjoint to restriction. Thus there are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal S)}(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal R)}(M,\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N).$$
The inverse sends $f$ to derived extension of $f$ followed by the action counit $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S\to N$. Restriction keeps the underlying complex, cohomology sheaves, and mapping cones. These constructions and their adjunction maps commute with restriction to open subspaces when the site is the open site of a space. The same assertions for left modules use the opposite algebras.

source.place: Tags 0FT4 (lemma-qis), 0FT5 (definition-derived-category and preceding localization construction), 0FTF (lemma-derived-tensor-product), and 0FTR (lemma-derived-adjoint-push-pull) for the identity geometric morphism; the underlying-complex restriction and action-counit normalization are the explicit dg scalar adjunction of section-dg-bimodules. Open restriction follows from the same good-resolution construction.

proof.text: For each algebra use [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-homotopy-system] to obtain its triangulated homotopy category and saturated triangulation-compatible class of quasi-isomorphisms. Form the category of fractions in the ambient universe of the size convention. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] and [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] give $D(\mathcal A)$ its triangulation, exact localization $Q_{\mathcal A}$, and the characterization of distinguished triangles as localized cone triangles. This does not identify dg modules with complexes in the abelian category of dg modules: those would be different complexes. Morphism sizes are taken in the ambient universe, not asserted to lie in the smaller coefficient universe.

Put $U=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$ and $F(M)=M\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S$. The right action on $UN$ is $n r=n\varphi(r)$. Thus $U$ keeps the underlying differential, all cohomology sheaves, homotopies, shifts and the displayed cone matrices. It inverts quasi-isomorphisms after $Q_{\mathcal R}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends it to $R$. Since every distinguished triangle is a localized cone triangle, $R$ is exact. On tensors the shift and cone comparisons for $F$ are identity maps on the $M$ summands; the differentials $d(m\otimes s)=dm\otimes s+(-1)^{|m|}m\otimes ds$ agree with the shift and cone matrices. A homotopy extends by $h(m)\otimes s$. Consequently $F$ is also an exact functor on homotopy categories.

source.place: sdga: section-dg-bimodules and section-derived-pullback before Tag 0FTF; direct cone and differential calculation.

proof.text: There is an ordinary homotopy-category adjunction $F\dashv U$: a map $g:FM\to N$ restricts to $m\mapsto g(m\otimes1)$, and its inverse takes $f:M\to UN$ to $m\otimes s\mapsto f(m)s$. Balancedness is $f(mr)s=f(m)\varphi(r)s$; the dg Leibniz rules show these are chain maps. The same formulas send a degree-minus-one right-linear homotopy to a homotopy, since the two terms involving $ds$ cancel with signs $(-1)^{|m|-1}$ and $(-1)^{|m|}$. The unit is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and counit is $n\otimes s\mapsto ns$; both triangle identities reduce to the unit action. These formulas are natural in both variables.

source.place: sdga: section-dg-bimodules and lemma-adjunction-push-pull-dg with identity geometric morphism.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the good right $\mathcal R$-modules of [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-good-resolutions]. Every module has a quasi-isomorphism from one. For a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to P'$ between good modules, its cone is good and acyclic by the two cited statements. Tensoring that cone with the left $\mathcal R$-module $\mathcal S$ is acyclic, even when $\mathcal S$ is not flat. The tensor cone comparison of step 2 identifies it with $C(Fp)$, so $Fp$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $Q_{\mathcal S}F$ inverts all quasi-isomorphisms between good modules.

Apply [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy] with $K(\mathcal R)$, its quasi-isomorphisms, $Q_{\mathcal S}F$ and the good modules. Step 4 verifies both hypotheses and step 1 gives the required right fractions and two-out-of-three. The resulting essentially constant denominator diagrams give pointwise right Kan extensions by [lem-pur-left-derived-defined-pointwise-kan-bridge]; [lem-pur-total-left-derived-localization] assembles them into $L$ with comparison $\alpha:LQ_{\mathcal R}\to Q_{\mathcal S}F$. On a good $P$, $\alpha_P$ is invertible. [lem-pur-left-derived-exact-when-defined] applies because $Q_{\mathcal S}F$ is exact and defined everywhere; it makes $L$ exact. Thus $L(M)$ is computed by $P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S$ for any good resolution $P\to M$.

The derived pair $(L,\alpha)$ is absolute: applying any functor to the cone, retraction and common-stage equalities defining an essentially constant pro-diagram preserves all those equations. The essential-constancy-to-Kan bridge therefore applies after every postcomposition. This uses the explicit definition [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram], not an unsupported absoluteness inference from a Kan extension. The functor $R$ is an absolute right derived functor of $U$: $Q_{\mathcal R}U=RQ_{\mathcal S}$ up to its fixed factorization, and precomposition with localization is fully faithful; this statement remains true after every postcomposition by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Apply the existing absolute derived-adjunction theorem [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] to step 3. It yields $L\dashv R$ and its natural Hom bijections. Its counit formula, using the factorization $RQ_{\mathcal S}=Q_{\mathcal R}U$, is $\epsilon_{Q_{\mathcal S}N}=Q_{\mathcal S}(n\otimes s\mapsto ns)\circ\alpha_{UN}$.

For a derived morphism $f:M\to RN$, its inverse Hom transpose is $\epsilon_N\circ L(f)$: naturality of the unit and counit and the two triangle identities show that this operation and $g\mapsto R(g)\circ\eta_M$ compose to the identity. On a good resolution $p:P\to UN$, the counit of step 6 is represented by $P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S\to N$, $x\otimes s\mapsto p(x)s$, using naturality of $\alpha$ and the inverse of $LQ_{\mathcal R}(p)$. Thus it is the derived action map, rather than an arbitrary choice of adjunction counit.

source.place: sdga: Tag 0FTR and section-dg-bimodules; counit computation from the derived comparison.

proof.text: On an open site, $j^*$ is restriction of the sheaves to smaller opens, so preserves the differentials, balanced tensor sheaves, actions and cone matrices. By [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-good-resolutions], $P|_V$ is good and $p|_V$ remains a quasi-isomorphism. For good $P$, define $\theta_P:j^*LQ_{\mathcal R}P\to L_VQ_{\mathcal R|_V}(P|_V)$ by $\alpha_{P|_V}^{-1}\circ j^*\alpha_P$, with the ordinary tensor restriction identification understood. It is invertible and natural for all maps between good modules. Apply [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class] to the two functors on $K(\mathcal R)$ and then to the inverse maps. Both functors invert quasi-isomorphisms. The two extensions are inverse: for any $p:P\to M$, naturality conjugates their composites to the identity at $P$. [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now descends this natural isomorphism to $D(\mathcal R)$. This proves compatibility on derived morphisms, not just on representing objects. Restriction $R$ commutes with $j^*$ literally on the underlying complexes.

source.place: sdga: section-P-resolutions, condition (3), Tag 0FSH; section-localization-dg; comparison on good representatives.

proof.text: The isomorphism of step 8 commutes with the adjunction maps. For the counit, choose $p:P\to UN$ good and use step 7: both restricted arrows send $x\otimes s$ to $p(x)s$. For the unit on a good $P$, the ordinary map $P\to UFP$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, followed by the inverse of $R\alpha_P$, represents the derived unit by the derived-adjunction construction. Its restriction is that same formula on $P|_V$. Naturality along a good resolution $P\to M$, which is inverted, proves the unit assertion for every $M$. The comparisons for nested opens coincide on good representatives and hence everywhere by the same naturality argument. Finally a left dg $\mathcal A$-module is a right dg $\mathcal A^{op}$-module via $m\cdot a=(-1)^{|m||a|}am$, where $a\star b=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$. Associativity and the Leibniz identity follow by adding these exponents. This correspondence preserves underlying cohomology, homotopies and cone matrices, so the preceding right-module construction gives all the left-module assertions.
